Basic version (checks the format only):

```regex
^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$
```

Stricter version, which limits months to 01–12 and days to 01–31:

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` is a four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is a month from 01 to 12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is a day from 01 to 31.
- `^` and `$` anchor the match so nothing else can be on either side. Drop them if you're searching for dates inside longer text, and use `\b` at both ends instead.

Both match `2026-10-01`. The regex can't tell which months are short or which years are leap years, so it accepts `2026-02-31`. If that matters, parse the date afterwards, for example with `datetime.date.fromisoformat()` in Python or `Date.parse` plus a round-trip check in JavaScript.
